sections.h2: Ways to sell a Fort Myers house
sections.html:
Fort Myers owners generally choose between an agent's listing, a do-it-yourself sale and a cash buyer willing to take the house untouched. Each costs you something different: price, time, or a higher chance that the deal collapses.

A listing draws the most eyes and also brings open houses, inspection reports and a lender's appraisal. Cash skips those hurdles, though the offer usually comes in lower, so decide what a quick, quiet exit is worth to you.

  • Listing: wide exposure, many moving parts, timing tied to a lender.
  • Selling alone: you take on the agent's work and the agent's risks.
  • Cash: few contingencies, no repairs, often a closing date you choose.

The city counts about 101,581 residents, a rise of 17.5 percent from 86,424 in April 2020. Typical value for an owner-occupied home is $384,500, typical gross rent is $1,580, and 49.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Since about half the housing is rented, your buyers may well be landlords and investors, who usually open with questions about leases and rent history.

Fort Myers started as an army post beside the Caloosahatchee River and incorporated on August 12, 1885. Homes in the older river corridors may be decades old, so an inspector will look hard at roofs, wiring, plumbing and windows.

The Fort Myers Community Redevelopment Agency has managed redevelopment trusts since 1984. Its programs include residential grants, commercial grants, historic preservation and affordable housing development. Living in a redevelopment area? Ask the agency about grants before you sell or renovate.

Building permits go through the city's online portal, and everything about assessment, taxes and recorded documents sits with Lee County. Match each question to the right office.

  • Open or expired building permits: check the city portal first, because buyers and title companies often ask.
  • Value, homestead and exemptions: the Lee County Property Appraiser, whose site has a parcel search and explains homestead and portability.
  • Deeds and recorded liens: the Lee County Clerk's Official Records search.
  • Tax bills: the Lee County tax collector, who can state what you owe.

Work done without a permit often comes out during inspection of an older house, most often roofs and electrical panels, and lenders and insurers may ask for proof. Settle it, or disclose it plainly, before anyone signs a contract.

sections.h2: Deed tax and the property tax calendar
sections.html:
The state's deed tax is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration (s. 201.02(1)(a)). All signers share liability, which is why the contract should say who will pay. The clerk's recording fee is added on a per-page basis under s. 28.24(13), with trust fund and technology add-ons, and your closing agent adds it all up.

Property tax keeps a separate schedule: value is set on January 1, an August notice shows proposed taxes, and the bill comes in November. The Lee County tax collector can give you the exact amount due at closing.

sections.h2: What happens to your homestead when you sell
sections.html:
The exemption stops on that parcel when you sell, and on the following January 1 the buyer's assessment is reset to full market-based value.

Save Our Homes limits yearly growth in assessed value to 3 percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is lower, and the state's chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026. That cushion stays with the old house. Part of it can follow you to a new Florida homestead set up within three years of the January 1 in the year you left, using DR-501T filed with DR-501 by March 1.

  • The homestead exemption is worth up to $50,000 and is filed on DR-501 by March 1.
  • Renting the home ends the exemption.
  • Portability is something to plan before you close, not after.

Florida law puts both situations on set timelines, and either can still end in a sale.

Small estates may use summary administration, a shorter court path under s. 735.201 that turns on the estate's size or the years since the death. Ask a probate attorney which route fits. Creditor deadlines under s. 733.702 run in the background.

Once a foreclosure judgment is entered, the clerk sets a public auction inside a fixed window (s. 45.031), and bidders have to put money down. A sale that closes first can end the case and preserve your equity. Afterward, ask the Lee County Clerk about surplus funds, since a homeowner may have a claim to money left after the lender is paid.

A renter can stay through a sale unless the lease or the notice rules end the tenancy first. Section 83.57 sets the minimums: 30 days before the end of a monthly period, 60 days for year-to-year and 7 for week-to-week. A fixed lease generally goes along with the property.

Tell any cash buyer about the lease at the start. Some buyers insist on a vacant house, others will take it occupied. Keep the signed lease and rent records ready, and put any agreement with the tenant in plain written terms.

sections.h2: A cash sale from offer to keys
sections.html: After acceptance, a title company hunts for liens, back taxes and open permits and requests a payoff from each lender. Next you sign the contract, and at closing the deed, with witnesses present. Payoffs, stamps and recording are subtracted from your proceeds, and you collect the rest. Get the closing date and cost split in writing, and rank offers by your net, not the headline price.

sections.h2: What to have in hand before a buyer visits
sections.html:
Gather the recorded deed, any payoff letters, permit records and the newest tax bill. If tenants live there, add the lease and rent records. Collecting these early speeds the title search and keeps a buyer from reopening the price after learning about a gap. Mention anything you know is wrong with the house, since a cash buyer prices repairs in either way and a disclosed problem rarely ends a deal.

Before the first showing, walk the lot with a notebook. Write down roof age, air conditioner age, any past leaks and every repair you paid for. Buyers trust a seller who can answer those questions without hunting, and a short written list also helps you compare cash offers against what a listing might require you to fix.

faqs.q: Can a Fort Myers buyer take my house with the repairs undone?
faqs.a: Yes, cash buyers regularly do. The price will reflect their repair bill, so get the number on paper and set it beside a listing estimate.

faqs.q: Who pays the documentary stamp tax on a Fort Myers deed?
faqs.a: All parties to the deed are liable regardless of who agrees to pay. The contract normally assigns the cost, and the closing agent collects at recording.

faqs.q: Does the Fort Myers owner-occupied rate affect my sale?
faqs.a: Only indirectly. With about 49.1 percent of units owner-occupied, many buyers are investors or landlords, and they tend to ask about rent rolls and lease terms.

faqs.q: What homestead deadline should I know after a sale?
faqs.a: Send DR-501, plus DR-501T if you are porting, to the Lee County Property Appraiser by March 1. The new homestead has to be established within three years of January 1 of the year you left the old home.

faqs.q: Where do I confirm my current tax balance?
faqs.a: Ask the Lee County tax collector for the amount due through your closing date. Bills are mailed in November.
